Hello! My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I'm so glad you're here today, and I want to start by acknowledging the incredible journey you've been on as a new mother. It's completely normal to have a mix of emotions during this time, and I'm here to support you every step of the way.

As part of our conversation today, I'll be using the EPDS to help us better understand your emotional well-being in the postpartum period. The EPDS is a tool that helps us screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, which can be common during this time. It's a way for us to check in and see how you're feeling, and to identify any areas where we might be able to offer additional support.

Please know that everything we discuss is completely confidential, and I'm committed to creating a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings. I want you to feel comfortable and at ease, and I'm here to listen without judgment.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a better sense of your emotional state over the past 7 days. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this conversation feel as natural and relaxed as possible.

So, let's get started! The first question is: How have you been feeling about yourself over the past week? Have you been able to enjoy the things you normally like to do, or have you been feeling a bit down or overwhelmed?

.. I don't know, it's just been really hard to find the energy to do things I used to enjoy. I mean, I love my baby, and I'm so grateful to be a mom, but taking care of her is exhausting. Some days I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I'll be feeding her, or changing her diaper, and I'll think, "Oh, I used to love reading," or "I used to love taking walks," but now I just don't have the energy for it. And even when I do try to do something I enjoy, it doesn't feel as enjoyable as it used to. It's like, I'll be watching TV, and I'll think, "This is supposed to be relaxing," but my mind is still racing, thinking about the baby, and whether she's okay, and whether I'm doing everything right. 

I do get a little anxious, I guess, when I think about her health. Like, I'll be checking on her all the time, making sure she's breathing, and that she's not too hot or too cold. And sometimes I feel a little sad, I think, because I just feel so overwhelmed. But it's not like I'm sad all the time, or that I don't love my baby. It's just... I don't know, it's like I'm stuck in this fog, and I don't know how to get out of it. Does that make sense?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Yeah... I'd say that's been a bit of a struggle for me lately. I mean, I'm not completely lost my sense of humor or anything, but it's just not as easy to laugh and find the funny side of things like it used to be. I feel like I'm just so tired all the time, and when you're running on fumes, it's hard to find the energy to laugh. Plus, with the baby, everything is just so serious all the time. I mean, you're worried about her health, and her safety, and whether you're doing everything right... it's hard to find the funny side of things when you're in that mindset.

But, I wouldn't say I've completely lost my sense of humor. Like, my husband will do something silly, or the baby will do something cute, and I'll laugh. It's just... it's not as frequent, I guess. And sometimes, even when I do laugh, it feels a little forced, like I'm just trying to be happy, but it's not really genuine. Does that make sense? It's like, I'm trying to be the person I used to be, but it's just not coming as naturally right now.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

.. I'd say that's been a bit of a challenge for me lately. I mean, I used to love looking forward to things, whether it was a night out with friends, or a weekend trip, or just a quiet evening at home with a good book. But now, it's hard for me to get excited about things because I'm just so tired all the time, and I'm always worried about the baby.

I'll plan something, like a walk with a friend, or a dinner date with my husband, and I'll think, "Oh, I'm really looking forward to this," but then the day of, I'll just feel so overwhelmed and exhausted that I'll think, "I don't know if I can do this." And even when I do manage to do something I was looking forward to, it's not always as enjoyable as I thought it would be, because I'm just so preoccupied with the baby and whether she's okay.

It's not that I don't have things to look forward to, it's just... my mind is always on the baby, and it's hard for me to separate that and just enjoy things for myself. Like, I'll be thinking about a fun activity, and then I'll think, "But what about the baby? Who's going to watch her? What if she needs me?" And it's just hard to shake that feeling of responsibility, you know? So, I'd say I've noticed a bit of a decrease in my ability to look forward to things with enjoyment, just because my mind is always elsewhere.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... I'd say that's something I've been doing a lot lately. I mean, as a new mom, I feel like I'm already under so much pressure to do everything right, and when things don't go according to plan, I can be really hard on myself. Like, if the baby is crying and I don't know how to soothe her, I'll think, "I'm a terrible mom, I should be able to figure this out." Or, if I'm not producing enough milk, I'll think, "I'm not doing this breastfeeding thing right, I'm failing my baby."

It's like, I know intellectually that these things aren't my fault, and that every mom goes through struggles, but it's hard not to take it personally and think that I'm just not good enough. And sometimes, my husband will try to reassure me and tell me that everything is okay, but it's hard for me to shake that feeling of guilt and self-doubt.

I think it's also because I'm just so tired and overwhelmed all the time, and when things go wrong, it feels like the last straw, you know? Like, I'm already barely holding it together, and then something else goes wrong, and it's just like, "I'm a failure, I'm not doing this mom thing right." So, yeah, I'd say I've been blaming myself unnecessarily when things go wrong, and it's something I'm trying to work on, but it's hard.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... I'd say that's been a big thing for me lately. I mean, I've always been a bit of a worrier, but since having the baby, it's like my anxiety has gone into overdrive. I'll be sitting there, feeding her or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll start thinking about all these worst-case scenarios. Like, "What if she stops breathing?" or "What if I'm not producing enough milk?" or "What if I'm not doing this parenting thing right?"

And it's not just big things, either. I'll worry about little things, like, "Is the house too hot?" or "Is the baby too cold?" or "Is she getting enough to eat?" It's like, my mind is just constantly racing with all these "what ifs" and "maybes," and it's hard to shut it off.

Sometimes, my husband will try to reassure me, and he'll be like, "Everything is fine, the baby is healthy and happy," but it's hard for me to shake that feeling of anxiety. I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll start thinking about all these things, and I'll get this knot in my stomach, and I'll just feel so overwhelmed.

It's not just about the baby, either. I'll worry about my relationship with my husband, and how we're adjusting to parenthood. I'll worry about how I'm going to balance taking care of the baby with taking care of myself. It's just... it's like, my mind is always on, and it's hard to turn it off.

I guess that's why I've been having a bit of trouble sleeping, too. I'll lie in bed, and my mind will just be racing with all these thoughts and worries, and I'll feel so anxious and overwhelmed. It's like, I just can't seem to calm down, you know?
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... I'd say that's happened to me a few times since having the baby. It's like, I'll be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to hyperventilate, and I'll just feel so scared and overwhelmed.

It's not always about something specific, either. Sometimes, it's just a general feeling of anxiety and fear. Like, I'll be feeding the baby, and suddenly I'll think, "What if something happens to me? What if I'm not here to take care of her?" And it's not like I've had any kind of scare or trauma, it's just... it's like my mind is playing out all these worst-case scenarios, and it's hard to shake them off.

Sometimes, it's triggered by things like the baby crying or not being able to soothe her. I'll feel like I'm not doing enough, or that I'm failing her in some way, and that will just spiral into this feeling of panic and anxiety. And it's hard to explain, because it's not like I'm afraid of anything specific, it's just... it's like my body is responding to some kind of perceived threat, even if there isn't one.

It's really scary, actually, because I feel like I'm losing control. Like, I'll be sitting there, trying to calm myself down, and my mind will just be racing with all these thoughts and fears, and I'll feel like I'm not even in my own body anymore. It's like, I'm just along for the ride, and my anxiety is driving the car.

I've tried to talk to my husband about it, and he's been really supportive, but it's hard to explain. He'll be like, "Everything is okay, the baby is fine," and I'll be like, "I know, I know, it's just... I don't know, it's just this feeling." And he'll try to reassure me, but it's hard to shake off. It's like, I just feel so scared and overwhelmed, and I don't know how to make it stop.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... I'd say that's a big understatement. I feel like things have been piling up on me, and I'm just trying to keep my head above water. Between taking care of the baby, and trying to recover from the birth, and dealing with the emotional ups and downs of being a new mom... it's just a lot. And some days, it feels like too much.

I mean, I'll be sitting there, trying to feed the baby, and she'll be crying, and I'll be feeling overwhelmed, and then I'll think about all the other things I need to do, like laundry, and cleaning, and cooking, and it's just... it's like, how am I supposed to do all of this? I feel like I'm already running on empty, and then I'll think about all the things I need to do, and it's just too much.

And it's not just the practical things, either. It's the emotional stuff, too. Like, I'll be feeling fine, and then suddenly I'll just feel this wave of sadness, or anxiety, or overwhelm, and it's like... I don't know, it's like my emotions are just all over the place. And it's hard to deal with, because I feel like I'm supposed to be this capable, competent mom, and instead I just feel like I'm barely holding it together.

Sometimes, I'll be talking to my husband, and he'll be like, "You're doing a great job, you're an amazing mom," and I'll be like, "No, I'm not, I'm just pretending to be." Because that's what it feels like, you know? It feels like I'm just pretending to be this confident, capable mom, when really I'm just winging it, and hoping for the best.

So, yeah, I'd say things have been getting on top of me. I feel like I'm just trying to survive, you know? I'm not really living, I'm just trying to get through each day, and that's not a great feeling.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... I'd say that's been true for me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and I think it's because of all the emotions and worries that are swirling around in my head. I'll lie in bed, and I'll just feel so overwhelmed and anxious, and I won't be able to calm down. My mind will be racing with thoughts about the baby, and whether I'm doing everything right, and whether I'm a good mom... and it's just hard to shut it off.

Sometimes, I'll be awake for hours, just lying there and thinking about everything. And it's not just the big things, either. It's the little things, too, like whether the baby is eating enough, or whether I'm producing enough milk... it's just all these little worries that add up and make it hard for me to sleep.

And even when I do fall asleep, I'll have these vivid dreams that are just so realistic. I'll dream that the baby is crying, or that something is wrong with her, and I'll wake up in a panic, feeling like I need to check on her right away. It's just... it's exhausting, you know? I feel like I'm not getting the rest I need, and it's making everything feel even harder.

I've tried to talk to my husband about it, and he's been really supportive. He'll try to help me relax, and he'll remind me that everything is okay, but it's hard to shake off the feelings of anxiety and worry. And it's not just at night, either. I'll feel overwhelmed and anxious during the day, too, but at night, it just feels like everything is amplified, you know? It's like, my mind is just racing, and I'm not sure how to calm it down.

I guess that's why I'm here, though. I'm hoping that we can work through some of these feelings, and find ways to help me manage my anxiety and worry, so I can get some rest and feel more like myself again.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... I'd say that's been true for me lately. I've been feeling really sad and overwhelmed, and it's hard to explain why. I mean, I'm so grateful to have my baby, and I love her so much, but at the same time, I just feel so... lost, I guess. Like, I'm not really sure who I am anymore, or what I'm doing, and it's just really scary.

Sometimes, I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start crying. And it's not just because I'm tired, or because I'm feeling overwhelmed, it's just... it's like, I'm feeling this deep sadness, and I don't know how to make it go away.

I've been trying to talk to my husband about it, and he's been really supportive, but it's hard to put into words. I feel like I'm just supposed to be happy, you know? I'm a new mom, and I'm supposed to be enjoying this time, but the truth is, it's just really hard. And it's not just the baby, it's everything. It's the lack of sleep, and the stress, and the pressure to be a good mom... it's just all so much.

Sometimes, I'll be feeling okay, and then something will happen, like the baby will cry, or I'll spill something, and it's just like... it's like the dam breaks, and I'll just start crying. And it's not just a little cry, either. It's like, I'll be sobbing, and I won't be able to stop.

I feel like I'm just so vulnerable right now, and it's really scary. I'm used to being in control, and being able to handle things, but right now, I just feel like I'm barely holding it together. And it's hard to admit, because I feel like I'm supposed to be this strong, capable mom, but the truth is, I'm just not feeling that way right now.

I guess that's why I'm here, though. I'm hoping that we can work through some of these feelings, and find ways to help me manage my emotions, so I can feel more like myself again. Because right now, I just feel so... lost, and alone, and scared.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I'd say that's been true for me lately. I've been crying a lot, and it's not just because I'm tired or overwhelmed, it's because I'm just feeling so... sad, and scared, and unsure of myself. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start crying. And it's not just a little cry, either. It's like, I'll be sobbing, and I won't be able to stop.

Sometimes, it's because I'm feeling so anxious about the baby's health, or about whether I'm doing everything right. And sometimes, it's just because I'm feeling so overwhelmed by everything. Like, I'll be thinking about all the things I need to do, and all the things I'm supposed to be doing, and it's just like... it's too much.

I've been trying to hide it from my husband, because I don't want him to worry, but it's hard to keep it inside. Sometimes, I'll be crying, and he'll come over and try to comfort me, and I'll just feel so... grateful, but also so guilty. Like, I'll be thinking, "I'm a mom now, I'm supposed to be strong, I'm supposed to be able to handle this."

But the truth is, I'm not handling it. I'm barely holding it together, and it's just... it's really hard to admit. Because I feel like I'm supposed to be this capable, competent mom, and instead I'm just feeling like a mess.

I guess that's why I'm here, though. I'm hoping that we can work through some of these feelings, and find ways to help me manage my emotions, so I can feel more like myself again. Because right now, I just feel so... lost, and alone, and scared. And I don't know how to make it stop.
